originalTitle: Is 'Trumpflation' real? Why Wall Street fears this could be a reason for stock market crash
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: the stock market has been doing very well lately, but some people on Wall Street are getting worried that it might start to do poorly. They're concerned about something called "Trumpflation", which seems to be related to rising prices and higher interest rates. The worry is that the group in charge of interest rates, called the Federal Reserve, might keep interest rates high or even raise them, which could hurt the stock market. This matters because higher interest rates can make it more expensive for companies to borrow money, which can affect their stock prices. If interest rates stay high or go up, it could cause the stock market to go down.

originalTitle: World Bank's IFC, HDFC AMC invest in Molbio Diagnostics' Rs 281 crore IPO anchor round
simplifiedContent: Molbio Diagnostics, a company based in Goa, is planning to raise money by selling shares to the public through an Initial Public Offering (IPO). Before the IPO opens on August 10, the company has already raised Rs 281 crore from important investors, including the World Bank's IFC and HDFC Mutual Fund. This is called an "anchor round" and it's a good sign for the company. The company will try to raise a total of Rs 940 crore from its IPO, and some big investment firms are recommending that people buy the shares. This investment from well-known organizations might make other investors more interested in buying Molbio Diagnostics' shares.

originalTitle: Market Trading Guide: Jindal Saw among 2 stock recommendations for Monday
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified version of the news: Some companies in the stock market have recently reported their earnings, and most of them have done as well as or even better than expected. This is giving investors hope for certain sectors of the market. As a result, some experts are recommending that investors consider buying specific stocks, including Jindal Saw, on Monday. This recommendation is based on the positive earnings reports and the potential for these sectors to do well. It may be a good time for investors to take a closer look at these stocks.

originalTitle: The stock market is finally rising again—and it’s getting cheaper, too
simplifiedContent: The stock market, which is measured by the S&P 500, has been doing well and has gone up by 22% over the past year. Even though the market is rising, the prices of stocks are actually becoming more affordable, which is known as valuations coming down. This means that investors can buy stocks at a relatively lower price compared to their earnings. This is a positive sign for investors, as it could indicate that the market is becoming more stable. The decrease in valuations suggests that the market's growth is not just due to inflated prices, but may be based on the actual performance of the companies.

originalTitle: Upcoming IPOs: Shiprocket IPO, Dhoot Transmission IPO among new issues to open next week; full list here
simplifiedContent: Some new companies, including Shiprocket and Dhoot Transmission, are going to start selling their shares to the public next week. This is called an Initial Public Offering, or IPO. The shares will be available for buyers to purchase between August 10 and 12. At the same time, shares from eight other companies that started selling last week will begin trading on the market. This means that investors will be able to buy and sell these new shares, which can be an opportunity for people to invest in these companies.

originalTitle: Defence stock Apollo Micro Systems declares Q1 results 2026. Revenue jumps 88% YoY to  ₹251 crore, PAT up 43%
simplifiedContent: Apollo Micro Systems, a company that makes defense products, just released its financial results for the first quarter of 2026. The company's revenue, which is the total amount of money it made from selling its products, increased by 88% compared to the same time last year, reaching ₹251 crore. Its net profit, which is the amount of money the company has left after paying all its expenses, also increased by 43% to ₹25.2 crore. This means the company is making more money from selling its products and is also keeping more of that money as profit. This is a positive sign for the company, and it may be interesting to investors who are considering buying or selling its stock.
